question: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts is used to insert 'Autosum', a quick and easy way of adding multiple values?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alt + =**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alt + =:** This is the shortcut for the Autosum function in spreadsheet applications like Microsoft Excel. When you have a range of numbers that you want to add together, you can select the cell where you want the sum to appear, then press Alt + =. Excel will guess the range you're trying to add and automatically create a formula to sum those values.
 
• **Shift + =, Tab + =, Ctrl + =: **these shortcut are not a universally established.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ctrl + C:** This is a universal shortcut used in most applications for copying the selected data. In Excel, you would use it to copy a cell's contents to the clipboard.
 
• **Ctrl + V:** This is another universal shortcut for pasting the data from the clipboard. In Excel, it would paste the contents you've copied into the selected cell.
 
• **Ctrl + Z:** This shortcut is typically used to 'Undo' the last action.
 
• **Ctrl + S: **This is most commonly used to save the current document or file.
 
• **F2:** In Excel, this is used to edit the active cell.
 
• **Ctrl +** **Arrow keys (left, right, up, down):** These shortcuts are used to navigate to the edge of the worksheet in the direction of the arrow.
 
• **Ctrl + Shift + Arrow keys: **These are used to highlight a range of cells in the direction of the arrow from the current cell.
 
• **Shift + Space:** This is used to select the entire row in Excel.
 
• **Ctrl + Space: **This is used to select the entire column in Excel.
 
• **Ctrl + 1: **This shortcut opens the 'Format Cells' dialog box.
